result.topic_en: Gauss finds the three remaining roots of a cubic by the substitution x = p − 1, computes them numerically, and concludes that only the root x = 4 is admissible as a 'letter number', which gives y = 14 and z = 13.
result.transcription:
Die drei andern Wurzeln sind enthalten in der Gleichung
$x^3 + 180xx + 366x + 182 = 0$
Schreibt man $x = p-1$, so wird sie
$p^3 + 177pp + 9p - 5 = 0$
deren Wurzeln
$p = +0,14451426$[?]
$p = -0,19553345$
$p = -176,94898$[?]
also
$x = $ [-$-0,85659$-] $-0,8554887$[?]
[-$-1,19608$-] $-1,1955330$
[-$-177,94900$-] $-177,9489782$[?]
Als Buchstabenzahl ist bloß die Wurzel
$x = +4$ zulässig, woraus
$y = +14$
$z = +13$
von selbst folgen.
1852 Sept 22

methods.what: Translating the variable (x = p − 1) to transform a cubic equation into another cubic
methods.quote:
Schreibt man $x = p-1$, so wird sie
$p^3 + 177pp + 9p - 5 = 0$

methods.what: Numerical values of the three real roots of the transformed cubic
Back-substitution to obtain the roots in x (a first, less accurate set struck out and replaced by refined values)
Selecting the admissible root (the only one that can be a letter number) and deriving the other unknowns
methods.quote:

$x = +4$ zulässig, woraus
$y = +14$
$z = +13$
von selbst folgen.
